value.title: Cache proxy watch: no false outage, stale upstream answers, seat-count notices
value.done_when: Plan 230 (docs/plans/230-cache-proxy-watch): a status read never waits on upstream and starts at most one background check; one slow watch read gives no notice, two in a row or a refusal give one; a gate read that times out is retried once; a 402 or 2xx answering a replaced token changes no state; notices give a seat count, never ids. Each guard has a test that fails without it, and the slow-upstream case is shown live on a private daemon and a test-port sidecar.
value.note: F204 (pm-001 LOG 2026-11-18: one slow probe made a false outage notice naming 43 seats), F205, the stale 402 latch (takin's s04 row 12 finding: a 402 sent before an account switch latched the new account), and count-only notices, notice noise of the F192 class (prime far-jackal: notices listed every proxied seat). Matrix row 12 is re-run in s04 after merge.

value.title: Stop tool-list flips on proxied seats; weigh per-seat TTL
value.done_when: Plan 232 (docs/plans/232-proxy-tool-flips) shows four things. (1) A proxied seat started after toolSearch=false keeps a flat tool list through bash, read_bash, extensions_reload and user turns. (2) The fleet is re-priced in egret's terms with the flips gone and the larger tool prefix paid for. (3) Per-seat TTL policies are weighed against 1h and 5m for all. (4) The live after-window is split by Copilot process start and re-run with at least 1h of post-restart data.
value.note: The fix is not code. It is `toolSearch: false` in the user-wide ~/.copilot/settings.json, applied by the prime (pij-far-jackal) on Jordan's go at 2026-11-19T03:27:46Z, because a repo cannot set it. Cause: Copilot 1.0.114's client-side generic tool search on the BYOK route added and dropped deferred tools, and every change re-wrote the whole prompt at the 1h price. The setting leaves residual flips, all priced as kept: extensions_reload token-only flips (canary 23fd00ea, 9da2c60e) and a +5-tool first change in one resumed process (e69a6a28, D-232-5). Re-priced against plain (egret's windows): achievable +8.5% before #243 and -11.2% after (a loss); optimistic bound +26.3% and +7.3%. Measured in the first hour after the setting: +11.8% in steady state, -7.3% with the restart re-writes included (n=474). Whether to keep the proxy is a prime/Jordan decision outside plan 232. Verdict: keep 1h for every seat; no per-seat TTL is built.

value.title: Seat route from its own evidence (F213)
value.done_when: A Copilot /restart of a proxied seat keeps it proxied, for every restart: at registration in a new process, a proxied route carries when its anchor, the stamped launch process (pid and start time), is among the claimed host's ancestors as the daemon reads them through the kernel parent chain, and the carried route keeps that anchor. Restarts are siblings under the first CLI, so the second and third restarts carry as the first does. The reason says 'carried from its proxied launch through a Copilot restart; route not re-read'. A reused or exited anchor, a process outside the lineage (quit-and-resume, reclaim) and a revive's own launch keep today's reading, and a route that turns plain drops its anchor; an opted-out seat stays opted out in any new process; a claim cannot supply a route or an anchor. Carried seats count in the outage notice and the doctor's lists. Each rule has a registration-seam test that fails without it.
value.note: F213: lark, parakeet and puffin read plain after /restart while their usage said isByok. Constraint (h), checked on a throwaway seat: Copilot runs extensions in a sandboxed host process (COPILOT_EXTENSION_SANDBOXED) that gets no COPILOT_PROVIDER_*, so a self-report from the extension is impossible. Reading the CLI's env from the daemon was rejected (pm-004: the whole env would pass through daemon memory, d-2/req-02, plus a launch per registration). Lineage costs no launch: it reuses the ancestry the native registration already verifies. Round 2 (live proof of #263): the second /restart read plain. Copilot's first CLI supervises: each restart is its fresh child and the previous restart's process exits, so restarts are siblings, not a chain; #263 matched the row's latest process, never the next restart's ancestor, and its unit test modelled a chain. The anchor (the stamped launch process, kept on the carried route) fixes it. Seats restarted before F213 read plain until revived (F221, won't fix). Residual: a future Copilot that dropped the env on restart would read carried-proxied while going direct.
